correctness.rationale: The claim fixes C=L(Q3), whose twelve vertices are the twelve cube edges, and defines Ind_2(C) by maximum induced degree at most one, not ordinary matching. I independently reconstructed all 2^12=4096 subsets and obtained exactly 456 faces, augmented f-vector (1,12,66,164,177,36). Following the stated exact pivot order (8,4,9,0,10,7,11,3,5,6,2,1) on the augmented face poset pairs 212 disjoint cover relations and leaves 32 critical four-vertex faces. Independent orientation and Kahn topological sorting of every one of the 1524 Hasse covers visits all 456 nodes and is acyclic. Because the empty face is matched, reduced discrete Morse theory gives an INTEGRAL wedge of 32 3-spheres rather than merely mod-two ranks; 4-dimensional facets do not obstruct this. I also reconstructed all 48 cube-affine permutations, checked that their full signed fixed-face Lefschetz sums yield the ten class values (32,2,8,10,2,0,4,-2,-1,1); total class-weighted trace 96 gives two B3-invariants and central inversion trace 10 gives eigenspaces 21 and 11. The cube itself can be reconstructed from the eight triangular cliques of the line graph, establishing the full automorphism group. All checks concern exactly this twelve-vertex graph.
residual_risks: The integral wedge relies on the standard augmented discrete-Morse acyclic-matching theorem, not on a separately supplied explicit CW attaching map; its exact hypotheses are satisfied.
The character is rational, not a full integral B3-lattice classification.

value.rationale: The cuboctahedron is a canonical rectified-cube graph, and its 2-independence complex is a mathematically natural edge-cluster analogue. A complete integral homotopy type of a nonpure 4-dimensional complex and its 48-element, ten-class homology character, including nontrivial 21/11 inversion splitting, are nonroutine equivariant topology data, not an arbitrary numerical slice. An exact finite invariant for a central polyhedral graph can stand alone without a claimed infinite-family theorem.
residual_risks: The classification is for one graph; extrapolation to hypercube line-graph families is unproved.
